value.body: The Financial Risk Manager (FRM) is a certification from GARP (Global Association of Risk Professionals), a US-based body. It covers market, credit, operational and liquidity risk, risk models and valuation, and is taken in two parts. In India it is seen mainly in banks, NBFCs, risk consultancies and the risk teams of global firms' Indian offices.

items.label: Exams
items.note: Computer-based, held in set testing windows

items.label: Enrolment fee
items.note: One-time, paid with the first Part I registration

items.label: Work experience
items.note: Needed to be awarded the FRM after passing both parts

value.title: How you get in
value.body: No degree is needed to register, so students can take Part I during or after college. Pass Part I, then Part II, then show two years of relevant full-time work experience to GARP to be certified.

value.title: At a glance
items: Fees are in US dollars, so the cost in rupees moves with the exchange rate.
Employers usually read it alongside a degree (B.Com, MBA, CA or similar) and work experience, not in place of them.
Common roles: market risk, credit risk, model validation and treasury risk.
Many candidates take it while working, since certification needs experience anyway.
